bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Cautiously optimistic; Emphasizes 'business as usual' for financials but 'strategic shift' for growth; Reluctant to quantify volume impact prematurely but confident in medium-term trajectory; Transparent about one-offs.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: The 'discharge system' is not a standalone product but an engineering layer that creates stickiness, allowing AIA to bypass commodity pricing discussions and antidumping hurdles by tying value to customer throughput gains (15%+ improvement).
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Ability to offer a total solution for mill grinding efficiency and reliability rather than standalone wear parts — explicitly named by management as a key differentiator versus competition
- Comprehensive product portfolio spanning mill liners, the New Generation Discharge System and grinding media, enabling cross-selling of grinding media into liner accounts
- Application engineering and metallurgy depth — ore characterisation, pilot mill testing, Bond Work Index studies, charge trajectory analysis and site audits used to design application-specific solutions
- Global service and distribution network — 120+ countries served, 130+ ports reached, 10+ warehouses, subsidiaries and representative offices across UAE, China, South Africa, Netherlands, Ghana, Indonesia, Australia and the UK, plus the Vega Industries marketing arm
- Efficient manufacturing facilities concentrated in India with automated, ISO-certified plants (manufacturing excellence and global supply chain and execution cited as differentiators)
- Over four decades of operating history in wear-resistant products, with an average director experience in the Company of 39 years
- Structural conversion opportunity: serviceable addressable market stated in excess of 2 million tonnes per annum in gold, copper and iron ore, where high-chrome mill internals penetration is put at not more than 25-30%
- Renewable energy capacity of 37.38 MW supporting cost and emissions control
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Trade barriers and anti-dumping duties in export markets — A major portion of sales is exported. Competitors able to manufacture high-chrome or forged balls locally file anti-dumping applications against the Company's imports, which management says is hampering business volumes and overall volume. Countries such as Mexico and the United States have imposed import duty on the Company's products, and the AR states plainly that where local governments protect local manufacturers "we are losing our market share in those Countries". The global shift from free trade toward protectionism is called out as a structural change, and elevated tariff barriers introduced since 2025 are described as having pushed average tariff rates to their highest levels in decades.
- Dependence on the mining cycle — particularly copper and gold — as the designated pillar of growth — Management lists "stability in the mining market particularly copper and gold" first among key risks. The growth thesis rests on converting mines from forged to high-chrome mill internals in gold, copper and iron ore, where penetration is stated at not more than 25-30%; a downturn in mine output or capex in those metals directly reduces the addressable consumable demand. Conversion also depends on trials currently running in the largest copper and gold mines of Chile, Peru and Ghana, whose outcome is explicitly conditional ("which, if successful, should establish the uniqueness of the solutions").
- Customer resistance to conversion and competition from local players — The AR states the Company has faced, for several years, competition from local players and "general resistance to change without substantial value addition in milling process". This is the demand-side constraint on the entire high-chrome conversion story and is why the Company has had to make transformative efforts to change its approach; slow conversion translates directly into flat volumes despite a large stated serviceable addressable market.
- Geopolitical volatility and supply-chain / freight disruption — Operating across the globe exposes the Company to war, terror attacks, political unrest and government default. The AR names the Iran-USA-Israel war, the Middle East situation, US trade policy changes and supply-chain disruptions, and flags disruption of the Strait of Hormuz — through which over 20% of world LNG, 45% of global sulphur exports and 30% of global methanol production pass — as a critical risk. Management says these may impact growth, delay cash inflows, increase procurement costs and raise currency volatility. Mitigation is advance production planning, higher inventory at warehouses in disrupted geographies, midterm shipping-line contracts and FOB-plus-actual-freight customer contracts, alongside a Business Continuity Plan and Disaster Recovery Plan.
- Foreign-exchange exposure and cross-border tax / transfer-pricing exposure — High export turnover combined with imported raw material exposes the Company to high volatility in multiple currencies; the dollar remained strong against most currencies through the year on higher oil prices. Separately, the Company carries potential tax exposure because tax authorities in various jurisdictions may take different views on cross-border transactions between affiliates and challenge the amount of profit taxed in their jurisdiction, which could increase tax expense including interest and penalties. Mitigated by a proactive and adaptive hedging policy and a dynamic pricing mechanism.
- Single-segment, single-product-family concentration with heavy export dependence — The Company primarily operates in only one segment — manufacturing of high chrome mill internals — with 100% of turnover from metal and metal products under a single NIC code (24319). In FY 2025-26, 64.45% of total sales came from outside India (BRSR states exports at 59.19% of total turnover), and manufacturing is concentrated in three plants, all in India. There is no product or geographic diversification to absorb a shock in the wear-parts consumable cycle or in export access.
- Credit risk on the investment portfolio and on export receivables — The Company deploys a large investible surplus in government and state government securities, AAA corporate bonds, commercial papers, fixed deposits and debt mutual funds; corporate bonds and debt mutual fund investments bear credit risk. Direct investments are restricted to board-approved AAA-rated corporates and debt mutual funds are monitored under an internal risk management framework. On the customer side, receivables are secured through LCs and bank guarantees and a comprehensive credit insurance policy has been taken to mitigate risks around the financial condition of export customers.
- Cyber security, data privacy and compliance across multiple regulatory jurisdictions — The business depends on complex, interdependent IT systems including internet and cloud-based systems and outsourced/collaborative systems requiring data exchange, making them vulnerable to breakdown, malicious intrusion and cyber-attack; failure to protect personal data may attract financial penalties, regulator intervention and reputational loss. Separately, operating in different geographies each with its own evolving regulatory landscape means any non-compliance can dilute financial position or jeopardise reputation. Mitigations cited include an information security policy, access control, multi-factor authentication, laptop encryption, annual VAPT, an IT disaster recovery plan, significant cyber security insurance, and a 'zero tolerance to non-compliance' governance philosophy.

business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: The Company manufactures a range of hi-chrome consumable wear parts — grinding media, mill liners and castings, collectively called "mill internals" — used in crushing and grinding in the cement, mining and thermal power industries. Its finished products are consumed as critical spare parts, and it increasingly sells a complete package of tailor-made solutions for SAG mills and ball mills combining mill liners (metal, rubber and composite), a proprietary New Generation Discharge System and high-chrome grinding media, backed by process diagnostics, application engineering and lifecycle support. Global marketing is carried out through Vega Industries, the Company's overseas marketing arm, supported by a network of subsidiaries, representative offices and warehouses.

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Transition from being a supplier of wear parts to a provider of integrated grinding solutions across the entire processing circuit — combining customised mill liners, high-chrome grinding media, process diagnostics, application engineering and lifecycle support into a single outcome-oriented offering.
- Focus on the mining industry as the pillar of growth, targeting conversion of mines from conventional forged products to high-chrome mill internals, where stated penetration is only 25-30% of a serviceable addressable market in excess of 2 million tonnes per annum in gold, copper and iron ore.
- Sell a complete package of tailor-made solutions for SAG mills and ball mills — mill liners (metal, rubber and composite) plus the Company's uniquely designed New Generation Discharge System — to improve mill operating efficiency, cut power costs and lift metal recoveries, and then cross-sell grinding media into those accounts as a natural corollary.
- Concentrate market focus on copper, gold and iron ore mining, with particular emphasis on expanding the footprint in South America including Chile and Peru, and on Ghana.
- Overcome anti-dumping duties and local-competitor pressure with a solution-based approach with mill internals rather than price competition, while defending positions with local consultants and following a fair-price / fair-margin policy (cited as having helped in Brazil and Canada).
- Strengthen and regionalise the global operating network — warehouses, subsidiaries and representative offices — to improve responsiveness, reduce supply-chain risk and maintain service continuity across key mining geographies.
- Reduce supply-chain and freight exposure operationally: plan production well in advance, hold higher inventory at warehouses in disrupted-supply-chain countries, pursue midterm contracts with shipping lines, and move customers to FOB-plus-actual-freight contracts.
- Fund growth from internal accruals and a robust liquidity framework, deploying investible surplus only in government securities, AAA corporate bonds, commercial papers, fixed deposits and debt mutual funds under a board-approved framework.
- Advance the sustainability agenda through renewable energy adoption, resource-efficiency initiatives and a structured ESG framework built on four pillars — Responsible Consumption, Responsible Practices, Responsible Communication and Responsible Supply Chain.
- Stated near-term priorities: expand the solutions footprint, deepen customer engagement, progress opportunities in key mining regions, and reinforce the global supply chain.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Capacity was held flat in FY 2025-26. The Company's current capacity stands at 4,36,000 MT per annum, stated as the position after closure of the Welcast plant at Bangalore, and the Chairman describes the year as one of "maintaining an installed capacity of 4,36,000 TPA" while incurring capital expenditure of ₹ 104 Crores. Production volumes for the year reached 255,820 MT against sales volumes of 2,58,002 MT. The manufacturing footprint is three clusters in India — Moraiya (capacity expanded to 2,60,000 MTPA in 2014), the Kerala GIDC greenfield grinding media facility near Ahmedabad (Phase 1 commissioned 2017, 50,000 MTPA added in 2019 and a further 50,000 MTPA of castings in 2023), and Odhav (20,000 MT of casting capacity added by de-bottlenecking in 2024) — supported by 10+ warehouses and 11 international offices. The most recent physical addition is the Rubber and Composite Liners Plant established at Kerala GIDC in 2025. Forward plans, all stated for FY 2026-27: (i) implementation of manufacturing plants in China and Ghana in a phased manner, under review for the past year but being approached cautiously given the geopolitical scenario, with the process to be expedited in the second half of FY 2026-27 if conditions normalise; (ii) an investment of ₹ 25 Crores to provide manufacturing flexibility to the recently commissioned Rubber and Composite Liners plant; and (iii) completion of the ₹ 30 Crore ambitious green energy project taken up during FY 2025-26 — a hybrid 33 MW scheme combining wind and solar power — which slipped from its expected H2 FY 2025-26 start and will now become operational from the beginning of Q2 of fiscal 2026-27, after which green energy is expected to rise to 30-40% of overall energy requirement and, from H2 FY 2026-27, 60-70% of total power consumed. Expansion is stated to be funded from internal accruals, with net cash of ₹ 612.54 Crore generated from operations in FY 2025-26. Existing renewable assets are 11 wind turbines plus 3 hybrid wind-and-solar projects at the Kutch and Jamjodhpur sites totalling 37.38 MW (31.80 MW windmill + 5.58 MW solar), currently meeting approximately 29% of overall electricity requirements — a level management says already exceeds its 2027 electricity target.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Mining demand: global electrification, renewable energy, energy storage, digital infrastructure and urbanisation continue to drive demand for critical minerals, particularly copper, gold and iron ore.
- Declining ore grades and harder ore bodies severely constrain grinding capacity worldwide, forcing miners to process lower-grade ore without sacrificing productivity — the structural driver management says its solutions address.
- Conversion headroom: high-chrome mill internals penetration is put at not more than 25-30% of a serviceable addressable market in excess of 2 million tonnes per annum in gold, copper and iron ore, offering significant headroom for conversion from forged products.
- Cement: infrastructure spending has largely plateaued in several developed economies, leading to relatively stable cement production and steady demand; high-growth markets such as India continue to see government-led infrastructure investment expected to drive higher cement consumption and demand for the Company's wear parts.
- Thermal power: the Company continues to enjoy a dominant position in the Indian thermal power industry, which is now poised to grow given the significant increase in power demand expected from massive planned data-centre investment in India.
- Mix and margin: the year's profitability was sustained through rigorous operational discipline, product mix optimisation and growing adoption of integrated grinding solutions across mining markets; EBITDA margin is stated at 39.46%.
- Geography: 64.45% of total sales in FY 2025-26 came from outside India and 35.55% from within India (single reported segment — manufacturing of high chrome mill internals).
- Headwinds: elevated tariff barriers since 2025, anti-dumping duties, import duties imposed by Mexico and the USA, freight volatility, and a strong dollar arising from higher oil prices are explicitly flagged as constraining volumes and market share in protected countries.
- Macro backdrop management works from: global growth projected below 3%, global headline inflation around 4.4%, US GDP growth around 2%, Eurozone practically flat, and India expected to grow at over 6% in FY 2026-27.
- Renewable energy adoption is expected to lower the energy cost base, with green energy rising to 30-40% of overall energy requirement and 60-70% of total power consumed from H2 FY 2026-27.
- Cash generation: net cash of ₹ 612.54 Crore generated from operations in FY 2025-26, stated as ensuring adequate resources to fund reinvestments and mitigate financial risks.
- A breakthrough in Chile — described as one of the world's most important mining jurisdictions — where the Company secured a large order for Grinding Media during the year (size not disclosed).
- Extensive trials underway in a few of the largest copper and gold mines in Chile, Peru and Ghana based on the new mining-liner solutions approach supported by the New Generation Discharge System; management is hopeful these will convert into sustainable business.
- Over the last three years the Company has successfully modified grinding mills in iron ore, copper and gold in more than 12 small to medium sized mills across different geographies.

open.item: Q4 realization ~178/kg (currency + product mix one-off); sustainable full-year realization ~165/kg going forward.
Renewables to supply ~60-65% of power once ~100 MW capacity comes online by June/July FY27.
Earlier ~15,000-ton South America (Chile) order dispatches started; regular invoicing stream from Q1FY27.
Second large-mine trial ongoing; outcome expected over the next couple of months.
Internal target to reach ~80% utilization of 440,000-ton capacity within 3 years (not a formal guidance).
FY27 outflow of 100-150 crores on maintenance capex and renewable balancing; ~30 cr balance to finish renewable portfolio.
Management believes volume can double from here over the next five years.
Continues holding high cash (~4,300 cr) despite ROCE drag; to consider reducing cash in 6-12 months.
Positions the liner + discharge-system + grinding media package as a unique multi-decade moat; design to be patented.
Operating margin (ex other income) ~28-29%; expected to trend to 24-26% as grinding-media mix rises with volume, though absolute profit grows.
China and Ghana plants (100,000 tons combined) on slowdown/paperwork status; can accelerate as needed, no firm timeline.
Global shipping volatility (transit +10-15 days) flagged as ongoing headwind but not a limiting factor; 100% pass-through.
Professional succession plan under implementation, to be formally in place over the next 1.5-2 years.
Acknowledges losing one large customer's volume to competition, a rare event; hopeful of correcting it.
Total capex for both China and Ghana plants estimated at USD 50 million using modular, automated technology.
Reiterates 1.5-2 million ton conversion opportunity intact; working on six-digit-ton opportunities across several mines.
Core strategy of converting the ~2.5 million ton forged grinding media market to high chrome, of which ~0.5 million already served by chrome.

verdicts.item: Expects to be back to 25,000-30,000-35,000 ton annual growth in a few quarters; rolling basis, FY25 as base.
verdicts.note: 'largely flat from full year last year' - growth run-rate not yet achieved.

verdicts.item: Declines to give FY26 volume growth guidance but reaffirms the 25,000-30,000 ton addition target is not abandoned.
verdicts.note: On FY27 'We are not giving any specific numbers... there are good things likely to come' - declines guidance while target not abandoned.

verdicts.item: China and Ghana plants delayed (land acquisition and approvals longer than estimated); plan/timeline update expected in next 1-2 quarters.
verdicts.note: 'Ghana as well as China are on a bit slowdown mode... under paperwork approval procedures' - timeline update provided.

verdicts.item: Confident of returning to normal growth from next fiscal (FY27); conversion news expected in coming quarters.
verdicts.note: 'We've gotten this important win' at a marquee South America customer; 'the volume journey for AIA will now start go forward... That is all our endeavor' - conversion news delivered, FY27 growth still…

verdicts.item: FY26 expected near-flat volume (between -5% and +15% vs last year); no specific growth guidance until end of Q2.
verdicts.note: 'full year sales of 258,000 tons, largely flat from full year last year, which was 255,000 tons' - within the -5% to +15% flat range.

verdicts.item: Hopeful of a South America (Chile copper) breakthrough in the next 2 quarters, flagged as a potential material game changer.
verdicts.note: 'we had a big breakthrough last month where one of a very marquee customer we implemented our solution'; 'they have immediately also given us the order for the second mine conversion' - breakthrough r…

verdicts.item: Mill liner business doing well, growing double-digit share of volume, with further expansions and investment.
verdicts.note: 'We have a good traction on the mill liners. We will only talk about the overall volumes' - no specific double-digit-share metric confirmed.

verdicts.item: US now carries ~9.6% ADD+CVD plus Section 232 tariff; customers paying the duty and business continues, but outcome uncertain.
verdicts.note: 'Status quo continues, as is' - US supply continues under duties.

verdicts.item: India capex outside the two overseas plants of ~100-130 crores (renewable, maintenance, land) for FY26.
verdicts.note: 'We spent about INR130 crores on capex' - within/near the 100-130 cr FY26 range.

verdicts.item: New modular grinding media plant in Ghana (up to 50,000 tons) for West Asian/gold market; expected over next ~18 months.
verdicts.note: 'Ghana as well as China are on a bit slowdown mode. However, we can accelerate as and when needed' - Ghana timeline pushed out.

verdicts.item: Ghana plant (50,000 tons) approval work to be largely done in next 3-4 quarters, then execution and commissioning.
verdicts.note: 'For Ghana, land and location is finalized'; 'under paperwork approval procedures' - approvals progressing but slowed.

verdicts.item: China plant (50,000 tons) expected up and about in some form in next 12 months; first phase operational by end of fiscal FY26.
verdicts.note: 'Ghana as well as China are on a bit slowdown mode' - end-FY26 China target not met.

wtt.summary: 48% guidance hit (32 chains); 2/11 projects on-time; 10% theme consistency (info)
wtt.tone_latest: Confident and upbeat on the proof-of-concept solution win and record profit; still declines volume guidance, owns that overseas plants and the second-mine trial are pending and the volume journey has yet to inflect.
